Peripheral neuropathy with nucleoside antiretrovirals: risk factors, incidence and management. Drug Safety 1998; 19: 481–94. Effects on the pancreas. Pancreatitis is recognised as being the most serious adverse effect of didanosine and can be fatal.1-3 It appears to be dose-related, occurring in up to 13% of patients receiving 750 mg of didanosine daily.2,4 Pancreatitis can resolve if didanosine is withdrawn5 and cautious reintroduction of dida- nosine has been possible in some patients.6 Raised amylase concentrations3 and glucose intolerance have been reported in patients who subsequently developed pancreatitis. 1.
